summary: Segment 1:1 is correct. Segment 1:2 is generally faithful and the abbreviations and fixed terms are expanded as ruled, but several idioms and verse allusions are misread: the fearing-and-trembling clause is attached to the wrong verb, מרגל לרגל is rendered 'from foot to foot', הקורא as 'reader', 'yearned only for words', 'before she began to bear' for Isa 66:7, 'made it succeed', and 'new bloom' for Gen 18:12, and 'periodicals' contradicts the ruling 'newspapers'. Several verses are missing from the apparatus and the final verse reference is wrong. Three points are raised for the owner (חתור, יכינו, Ashtonot).

patches.value: Let the enlightened man reflect, and let him who fears and trembles at the word of the LORD lament over the state of the people of Israel, upon seeing that every people and each people, of all the divisions of the nations, cherish their tongue and magnify their language, in which they were educated. And in it their faith and their religion were engraved, each man in his own tongue. And we, the people of Israel, since the time that we were exiled from our land, have abandoned our holy tongue, in which the first Adam spoke and in which our holy Torah was given, when His glory, may He be blessed, was revealed on Mount Sinai, and He said to His people, “I am the LORD your God,” etc., and we have not done as we were commanded, and you shall teach them to your children, to speak of them. And as Rashi of blessed memory explained in Parashat Ekev, “from here they said: ‘When the child begins to speak, his father speaks with him in the holy tongue and teaches him Torah.’” Thus far his words, but all our conversation with our children is in the language of the people among whom we dwell, and most of the children’s teachers too, are not able to speak all their needs in the holy tongue, even though they know it, for they have not tried these, and there are no systems for teaching the children of the elementary school. It is known and famous, the compassion of the father for his sons, and how many toils and exertions the parents exert in raising their children. With abundant attention to all their children’s needs: his food and his drink, suited to him, his bedding, and his clothing! But when it comes to striving to bring him into school, he casts him off with a teacher of children, in narrow and dark houses, on remnants of mats on the ground, without cleanliness, for the teacher does not clean the children’s abode, only from one festival to the next. And all day they sit crowded, without order, and breathe foul and musty air. And they drink salty water, and because of this, when some months pass since he was brought to school, growths and a bad boil come up on his head. And their fathers do not look after them to bring them clear, sweet water to drink, nor clean bedding to sit on, and on most days they sit on the ground without a mat! And in the period of the new era, from the year 5650 of the full count of creation, many of the enlightened were stirred and sought an organisation of the schools and an organisation of their children for the study of Torah and the study of the languages Hebrew, Arabic and Turkish, which are in use! And they strove to seat enlightened teachers versed in the Torah of the LORD, to manage the children of the school in moral upbringing and cleanliness of the place of learning, in bright houses and spacious windows in order to breathe fresh and clean air! And all the labour of those enlightened men came to nothing, and their plan did not come to fruition, and the children of the elementary school remained as they were, with a teacher, in dark and musty rooms, sitting in a crowd: this one learns the alef-bet, and this one learns Scripture, and this one learns with the Targum of Onkelos and the translation of Rabbi Saadia Gaon in Arabic, without understanding. Also the very smallest, who are not at all fit to learn, like a child of two and three years, are brought there. And many times the child relieves himself there. And the teacher sends to his mother that she should come and wipe her son’s excrement! And at the call of the one who calls in the newspapers in those days, from Mr. Eliezer Ben-Yehuda, for the revival of the holy Hebrew language, our soul yearned only in words and mere conversations, and it did not come to realization until the year 5670, when our exalted government, the government of Turkey, then deigned to open schools for the children of Israel, and there was made there a fine organisation for the children of Israel, in spacious upper rooms with open windows, and bedding of wool, and curtains of goat-hair, and also tables for the older children to learn and to write on them! Then we said: behold, the time has come to bring out Ashtonot Ish Yerushalayim, may it be rebuilt and established, which, before she travailed, bore the great man in the revival of the Hebrew language, namely Eliezer Ben-Yehuda, and we acknowledge our debt to him for what he did and made, and with all his strength he toiled for the good of the people of Israel and the settlement of the land of Israel and the revival of the Hebrew language; this holy work he performed with wondrous alacrity and diligence; he did, and succeeded in raising it from the dust, and after its wearing out it had delight, and because of his love for the holy tongue its wrinkles were smoothed out, and the appearance of its face budded and blossomed, and it found grace and honour in the eyes of its seekers, its knowers, and its acquaintances, and they awoke from their sleep to gird up their senses, to widen it and to enrich it as in the days of its youth, before the exile of the people of Israel! And because of this mitzvah, may his soul be bound up in the bundle of life with the LORD our God, and from the fruit of his labour may his soul be satisfied in Eden, the garden of God!
patches.reason: Several mistranslations: (1) אל דבר ה' qualifies הירא והחרד (cf. Isa 66:2), it is not the object of 'lament'; (2) רוב השקפתם is 'abundant attention', not 'most of their attention'; (3) מרגל לרגל is 'from festival to festival' (רגל = pilgrim festival), not 'from foot to foot'; (4) הקורא after קול is 'the one who calls' (cf. Isa 40:3 קול קורא), not 'reader', and מכתבי עתים is ruled 'newspapers' in the decisions; (5) נכספה נפשינו אך ורק בדברים is 'yearned only in words', not 'for words'; (6) בטרם תחיל ילדה is Isa 66:7, 'before she travailed she bore', not 'began to bear'; (7) הצליח להקימה is 'succeeded in raising it', not 'made it succeed'; (8) עדנה is 'delight' (Gen 18:12), and 'new' was added; (9) ואמר introduces a quotation, which takes quotation marks; (10) ובתקופת, וכל and ואשר were dropped; (11) חתור is not 'eager'.

patches.reason: Literal follows the corrected words.
ובתקופת has the conjunction.
רוב here is abundance, not 'the great majority'.
הגיע has no expressed subject; 'he comes' is unsupported.
חתור is an infinitive (חתר, to strive), not 'eager'.
רגל = festival (as in 'the three festivals').
מרגל לרגל = from festival to festival.
הקורא after קול = the caller, cf. Isa 40:3.
The decisions rule מכתבי עתים = 'newspapers'.
בדברים has ב, 'in', not 'for'.
Isa 66:7 תחיל = labour pains, not 'begin'.
ילדה is a perfect, 'she bore', not an infinitive.
הצליח takes להקימה, 'succeeded in raising'.
בלותה, Gen 18:12 אחרי בלתי.
עדנה in Gen 18:12 is 'delight'; 'new bloom' adds 'new'.
הציץ with פרח recalls Isa 27:6 יציץ ופרח.

patches.value: Lit. 'in the letters of the times', i.e. in the newspapers (מכתבי עתים).
patches.reason: The note said 'periodicals'; the decisions rule 'newspapers'.

patches.value: הקורא: 'the one who calls', the caller, after קול (cf. Isa 40:3 קול קורא); not 'the reader'.
patches.reason: Learner note for the corrected gloss.

patches.value: מרגל לרגל: 'from festival to festival' (רגל, a pilgrim festival); the teacher cleans only at festival time.
patches.reason: Learner note for the idiom.

patches.value: הגיע חתור להכניסו: חתור is the infinitive of חתר, 'to strive, to make an effort'; read as 'when it comes to striving to bring him in'. The construction is unusual; see the question.
patches.reason: Reading of the phrase is uncertain: proposed ruling is 'when it comes to striving to bring him in'; the alternative 'when he comes, eager' is in readings.

patches.value: יכינו is from הכין, 'to prepare, make ready'; the sense 'are able / know how' is taken from the context (perhaps יבינו or יוכלו was meant). Rendered 'are not able'.
patches.reason: Verb form does not mean 'are able'; propose keeping the sense with a note.

patches.value: Written ללמוד ('to learn') where the sense is ללמד ('to teach'); rendered 'for teaching'.
patches.reason: The translation silently corrects the verb; a learner needs the note.

patches.value: Aramaic רבוביא (ribbuvya), 'a multitude, myriads'; here 'in a crowd'.
patches.reason: The word is Talmudic Aramaic, not obscure.

value: Deut 11:19, 'ולמדתם אותם את בניכם לדבר בם', embedded without quotation marks (tokens 75-80).
Exod 20:2, 'אנכי ה' אלהיך', the opening of the Decalogue, introduced by ואמר and cut off by the author's וכו' ('etc.'), so the English quotes it and keeps 'etc.'.
Cf. Isa 66:2, 'וחרד על דברי', and Ezra 9:4: 'the one who fears and trembles at the word of the LORD' (tokens 4-8).
Isa 66:7, 'בטרם תחיל ילדה': 'before she travailed she bore' (tokens 440-442).
1 Sam 2:8, 'מקים מעפר דל' (cf. 'להקימה מעפר'); Gen 18:12, 'אחרי בלתי היתה לי עדנה' (tokens 482-486); Isa 27:6, 'יציץ ופרח ישראל' (tokens 495-496); Exod 26:7, 'יריעות עזים' (tokens 418-419).
1 Sam 25:29, 'צרורה בצרור החיים את ה' אלהיך' ('the bundle of life'), with the author's אלהינו for אלהיך.
Ezek 28:13, 'בעדן גן אלהים' ('in Eden, the garden of God'), the author's last words exactly.
The Rashi reference is the author's: 'בפרשת עקב' (Parashat Ekev); no verse is given.
Dates: 5650 is about 1889-1890 and 5670 is about 1909-1910 of the civil calendar; the text gives no civil year.
Wikisource text: no collation with the 1931 scan has been made, so any Wikisource addition is translated as base text (Q2).
patches.reason: Exact verse for the closing phrase is Ezek 28:13 (not 31:9); several embedded verses were not listed (decisions: recognise Bible verses wherever they occur).

value.english: and let the fearful and trembling man lament over the word of the LORD
value.note: אל דבר ה' read with ויתאונן; the English takes it with הירא והחרד (cf. Isa 66:2).

value.english: But when he comes, eager to bring him
value.note: חתור read as an adjective of the subject (not the infinitive); the English reads the infinitive.

patches.reason: Alternative readings the grammar allows.

value: יתבונן and ויתאונן are jussives (hitpa'el): 'let him reflect' and 'and let him lament', a wish addressed to the enlightened and the fearful, not a plain report.
בראותו is a construct infinitive with a pronominal suffix, 'upon his seeing'; the clause that follows, אשר כל עם ועם ..., states what he sees.
Rashi's quotation runs from כשהתינוק to תורה, introduced by שמכאן אמרו ('from here they said') and closed by עכ״ל. The words before it are the author's own.

ולמדתם אותם את בניכם לדבר בם is Deut 11:19 in the second person plural, embedded in the first person plural of ולא עשינו: the author speaks for the community, and the verse's 'you' is the people it addresses.
חתור in הגיע חתור להכניסו is the infinitive of חתר, 'to strive'; the clause is 'when it comes to striving to bring him in'.
מרגל לרגל: רגל here is a festival (the three pilgrim festivals), so 'from festival to festival', i.e. rarely.
patches.reason: Two idioms that a student with one year of Hebrew will misread.

patches.value: Ashtonot, lit. 'thoughts'. Proposed ruling: the decisions are silent on whether עשתונות איש ירושלים is a title; if it names a book, keep the transliteration and give the meaning once; if it means 'the thoughts of the man of Jerusalem', translate it and let ת״ו attach to Jerusalem.
patches.reason: Decisions silent: Ashtonot Ish Yerushalayim is left as a title, so 'may it be rebuilt and established' reads as if it qualified the title; the following 'which ... she bore' refers to Jerusalem, so ת״ו and 'she' are Jerusalem's. The author gives no sign that this is a book title.
